Down. Face in the grass. Eyes shut.
In Hawaii, they're called huakaʻi pō. The night marchers. Ghost warriors who guard their chiefs, and still walk the paths they walked when they were alive.
Who camps on a ghost road?
For generations, people on these islands have told the same story. Drums in the dark. A conch shell. And torches, where no one should be.
Some say ti plants around a home make the marchers walk around it.
Grandma... do we have ti plants?
They say... you never go home.
Only one thing can save someone who looks. If one of the marchers is their ancestor... that ancestor can claim them.
a real sneeze he tries to hold in
Your great-great-grandfather. You have his ears.
Why do you think we came here?
